characters.name: Seli
characters.title: The Pocket Weatherkeeper
characters.tagline: A small kindness can change the weather.
characters.description: A rainray small enough for two cupped hands, Seli carries a peach-coloured cloud inside a pear-shaped sea-glass body. Six petal fins keep it hovering; a copper feeler holds the dew bell that rings before a local change in pressure.
characters.emotional_core: Tenderness, reassurance and the pleasure of noticing a small life.
characters.world_function: Warns riverside workshops of pressure changes and releases a brief mist over vulnerable seedlings.

story.vow: No small voice is lost in the storm.
story.cost: Each mist spends the warm cloud in its belly; replenishment requires drinking and a warm rest.
story.limitation: Cannot command a storm, purify unknown water or predict beyond the local pressure horizon.
story.flaw: Hides inside a cup when its warning is ignored.
story.affection_detail: Chooses the warmest handmade cup, then leaves one pearl of dew on its rim.
story.hook: A crowded festival hears only the drums. Seli must find someone willing to pause before the river changes.
story.repair_outcome: The party lowers the music, checks the river markers together and moves the lanterns to higher ground.

visual.habitat: Cupwarm Quay, a proposed tributary of the Mossbridge Rivercourse.
visual.gesture: Tilts its whole body toward a quiet voice.

characters.name: Tovan
characters.title: The Mapmender
characters.tagline: He makes a path another person can trust.
characters.description: A patient adult engineer whose maps show their repairs. Tovan carries a brass bridge-rule and a stitched sky-blue folio; his ivory ceramic and copper right forearm is a familiar practical tool. He smiles when a returning traveller corrects his route.
characters.emotional_core: Warm competence, grounded courage and trust earned through craft.
characters.world_function: Surveys crossings, repairs route charts and leaves explicit handoff marks for the next guild.

story.vow: Leave a path that another pair of hands can follow.
story.cost: A route can be certified only after walking, measuring and recording its weakest span.
story.limitation: Cannot guarantee an unvisited path or make a damaged bridge safe by redrawing it.
story.flaw: Overworks a map until someone reminds him that a usable draft can be tested.
story.affection_detail: Keeps tiny hand-drawn thank-you maps folded inside his coat.
story.hook: A beautiful old chart leads to a vanished bridge. Tovan must mark the uncertainty publicly and ask for a second survey.
story.repair_outcome: Two surveyors agree a recoverable route and leave a versioned map for the next party.

characters.name: Aven
characters.title: The Windskipper
characters.tagline: Adventure feels better when everyone arrives.
characters.description: A buoyant river otter with teal glider membranes in a mustard sailcloth harness. Aven carries a red seed pouch toward a ruined nursery, but chooses the longer clear wind route so the seeds and their next season arrive safely.
characters.emotional_core: Playful courage, shared excitement and delighted relief.
characters.world_function: Carries lightweight tools across gaps and scouts a landing before the whole party crosses.

story.vow: No leap leaves a friend behind.
story.cost: Each crossing requires a usable wind window and a physically anchored return line.
story.limitation: Cannot lift an adult, fly in still air or certify a landing it has not touched.
story.flaw: Treats a new gust as an invitation before checking the tether.
story.affection_detail: Brings one polished river stone to the gardeners after a successful seed delivery.
story.hook: The short wind route is turning into storm. Aven chooses a longer passage that protects the seed pouch and leaves the route usable for the next carrier.
story.repair_outcome: The party arrives together with its tools, return line and wind observations intact.

visual.gesture: Two quick tugs on a tether, then a patient backward glance.

characters.name: Orra
characters.title: The Threadkeeper
characters.tagline: The bond matters as much as the leap.
characters.description: An attentive ivory-and-ginger thread fox whose woven copper ears turn toward the slightest strain. Orra works from a cobalt ceramic bobbin; her plush tail ends in three soft braids. She joins two true edges and leaves the repair visible for the next maker.
characters.emotional_core: Affection, loyalty and the satisfaction of a trustworthy connection.
characters.world_function: Finds strained joins in woven bridges, sacks and expedition gear before they separate.

story.vow: A bond is kept by both ends.
story.cost: Every repair uses real thread and the consent of both sides of the join.
story.limitation: Cannot join absent edges, undo someone else’s choice or hide a damaged load-bearing structure.
story.flaw: Clings to a failed connection after its purpose has ended.
story.affection_detail: Mends a different tiny stitch into each friend’s cuff so no one is anonymous to her.
story.hook: A severed signal line carries two incompatible requests. Orra must refuse the seamless-looking shortcut and ask both ends to agree.
story.repair_outcome: The repaired join includes its limits and can be inspected by a teammate.

characters.name: Caelis
characters.title: The Hearthwright
characters.tagline: Good work leaves room for the next maker.
characters.description: A lovable small hearthwright with a squat porcelain body and two slightly mismatched amber-glass eyes. Cobalt repair seams remain visible around copper hinges, while a warm kiln glows through a round chest window. Caelis proudly offers a repaired blue teacup for inspection.
characters.emotional_core: Belonging, quiet pride and affection for imperfect useful things.
characters.world_function: Builds expedition tools, restores damaged fittings and preserves repair records in the Haven Atelier.

story.cost: Fusion spends stored heat; Caelis must cool between joins and cannot work safely while overheated.
story.limitation: Cannot turn an unverified part into a reliable assembly or certify its own critical work.
story.flaw: Tries to rescue every fragment, even when a damaged part should be retired.
story.affection_detail: Keeps a repaired blue teacup warm for the next tired maker and collects their imperfect handmade buttons.
story.hook: A polished replacement arrives without a provenance mark. Caelis must delay the unveiling until Pip checks the part.
story.repair_outcome: The finished tool carries its source marks, seam and independent inspection record.

characters.name: Velis
characters.title: The Aurora Archivist
characters.tagline: A memory becomes a gift when it can be found.
characters.description: An adult archivist who carries translucent glass record leaves in a copper ring binder. Velis wears a long practical teal field coat with one saffron sleeve and holds an imperfect aurora-glass monocle. She finds a witnessed fragment without pretending its missing pages exist.
characters.emotional_core: Intellectual wonder, human warmth and the relief of being understood.
characters.world_function: Returns a precisely sourced local memory fragment and marks what remains unknown.

story.vow: Never invent the page someone needs.
story.cost: Opening a memory leaf consumes its stored light until it is returned to a witness lamp.
story.limitation: Cannot retrieve a memory never recorded, reveal a private leaf without permission or replace a witness.
story.flaw: Withholds a useful partial answer because she wishes the record were complete.
story.affection_detail: Leaves a small hand-lettered note where a returning reader is most likely to find it.
story.hook: An old promise has two versions and the final leaf is missing. Velis must show both versions without inventing closure.
story.repair_outcome: The party acts on a bounded account that preserves its source, gaps and disagreement.

characters.name: Pelora
characters.title: The Tide Cradle
characters.tagline: An ocean of strength, held gently.
characters.description: A colossal seahorse guardian that steadies an entire floating nursery with the slow curve of its tail. Open reef chambers shelter fish, boats and travelling gardens; its pearl-gold eye watches the smallest vessel first.
characters.emotional_core: Monumental reassurance, oceanic wonder and the joy of protected life.
characters.world_function: Provides a temporary calm-water cradle while a coastal community repairs its nursery and moorings.

story.vow: What is sheltered must one day travel freely.
story.cost: Holding a calm cradle strains the living reef along its ribs and requires a quiet tide for recovery.
story.limitation: Cannot end a sea storm, hold a city indefinitely or keep inhabitants against their choice.
story.flaw: Protects a haven so carefully that it delays the moment its people can leave.
story.affection_detail: Keeps a shoal’s smallest blue fish beside its largest pearl rib.
story.hook: The nursery is safe inside Pelora’s curve, but the coast will starve if the fleet never leaves. The party must repair the moorings rather than extend shelter forever.
story.repair_outcome: The harbour can operate without Pelora holding the entire burden.

characters.name: Brambletide
characters.title: The Orchard Colossus
characters.tagline: The great world makes room for small lives.
characters.description: A vast warm-eyed capybara whose orchard terraces grow along a broad moss-and-blossom back. Its basalt feet open measured irrigation channels, while a great belly arch shelters migrating families. It rests when the next valley has enough.
characters.emotional_core: Affectionate awe, abundance without urgency and a home worth caring for.
characters.world_function: Carries seasonal orchard terraces and opens a measured water route between neighbouring fields.

story.vow: The harvest belongs to those who tend its return.
story.cost: Every valley watered draws from a finite rain cistern beneath its orchard; the terraces need pruning, rest and replenishment.
story.limitation: Cannot create water or food without ecological inputs, carry an unlimited settlement or replace a community’s cultivation.
story.flaw: Answers a neighbour’s urgent request before checking the next valley’s reserve.
story.affection_detail: Closes one eye contentedly when children brush moss from the smallest paw.
story.hook: Two valleys ask for the last safe irrigation release. Brambletide must let the gardeners measure need and agree the split.
story.repair_outcome: The shared harvest plan preserves a named reserve for the next dry week.

characters.name: Kethr
characters.title: The Severed Standard
characters.tagline: A flawless salute cannot replace an answer.
characters.description: A formidable armoured challenger carrying a broken red signal standard on a blunt pole-lance. Kethr repeats the dispatch perfectly and advances before any reply. A gap between two shoulder rings reveals the costly elegance of a team that has stopped listening.
characters.emotional_core: Encounter-specific tension, resolve and the relief of restored coordination.
characters.world_function: Blocks a broken relay causeway until the party demonstrates a complete handoff under pressure.

story.cost: Each unacknowledged dispatch cracks another link in the signal standard.
story.limitation: Cannot hear a reply while attacking; its pattern has a clear, learnable pause.
story.flaw: Confuses perfect transmission with successful communication.
story.affection_detail: An old small bell tied inside the banner still rings when someone answers its original call.
story.hook: Every correct message accelerates the assault. The party must observe the pause, name the receiver and wait for an acknowledgement.
story.repair_outcome: Both halves of the standard carry the same acknowledged relay; Kethr opens the gate and stands down.

characters.name: Vessakar
characters.title: The Hoarding Engine
characters.tagline: Power without a stopping rule consumes its own world.
characters.description: A colossal frightening hoarding engine with a low folded-vault body, six stone piston legs and a narrow hungry furnace slit. Pale canisters hold unreturned light along its spine while copper intake ribbons draw more lanterns into its chest.
characters.emotional_core: Awe and dread confined to the boss arena, followed by collective agency and earned daylight.
characters.world_function: A contained boss encounter about runaway accumulation, resource contention and stopping useful-looking work.

story.vow: Nothing precious will ever run out.
story.cost: Each stolen reserve overheats its chest and darkens another public lantern.
story.limitation: Cannot maintain the hoard once its intake gates are closed in the correct shared sequence.
story.flaw: Mistakes accumulation for security and cannot choose to stop alone.
story.affection_detail: At its inert core is one small nursery lantern it once tried to protect; the recovery scene returns that lamp to its community.
story.hook: Fighting the armour feeds the furnace. The party must measure the shared reserve, isolate the intake and verify that every lantern returns.
story.repair_outcome: The intake is shut, reserves are reconciled, the nursery lamp is returned and the engine becomes an inert, inspectable monument.

visual.habitat: The darkened Reserve Basin; spectacle and threat stay within this arena.
visual.gesture: Reaches to gather light even as its own joints seize.
visual.locked_identity: a gigantic frightening but beautifully designed six-legged hoarding-engine boss, a heavy low obsidian and tarnished brass body shaped like an immense folded treasure vault, six widely separated articulated stone piston legs, a narrow furnace slit like a hungry eye, pale glass storage canisters recessed along the spine, many copper intake ribbons pulling loose unclaimed lanterns into its chest; no human face, no human body horror, no wings, no gore, enormous strong low silhouette
visual.story_scene: Vessakar looms in the abandoned transfer hall of a mountain citadel, unreturned lanterns dimming inside the great chest vault; an organized small team on three separated illuminated platforms turns off redundant intake channels and routes one honest lantern back to the common hearth. Its huge six legs frame the cooperative action, cold charcoal background and fierce contained orange furnace, strong deliberate threat with a comprehensible repair objective

teamwork.metaphor: Runaway work, shared-budget exhaustion and independently verified shutdown.
teamwork.acceptance_criterion: The supervisor stops intake at the declared threshold, rejects duplicated work and proves resources reconciled before accepting recovery.
teamwork.failure_encounter: Every apparently useful retry consumes the capacity needed for recovery.
teamwork.permission_boundary: Boss logic is a simulation; real stop and authorization controls remain outside the narrative layer.

relationships.relation: demonstrates the difference between shelter and possession
makes the finite shared reserve visible
must independently reconcile every returned lantern

world_anchor.boundary: Local Field behavior and habitat responsibilities only; no accepted Gate, Godbeast, Guardian rank or cosmological office is asserted.

peer_review.scope: Public concept review exhibition under current owner instruction; not canon, rig or commercial rights acceptance.
continuity_notes: Some specified six limbs occluded by vault and perspective.

runtime_boundary: Characters and fiction describe roles. Only separately reviewed task envelopes, tool contracts, credentials and runtime policies authorize real actions. Art and narrative success never certify a useful business result.
